newsitem.title: MEXICO: Democracy clause no hurdle in EU-Mexico deal-papers.
newsitem.headline: Democracy clause no hurdle in EU-Mexico deal-papers.

text.p: A key clause on democracy and human rights will pose no sticking point in negotiations for a trade agreement between Mexico and the European Union, papers quoted officials as saying.
Mexico is negotiating a potentially lucrative trade accord with the EU, whose insistence on the clause bogged talks down for months before Mexico agreed to the condition in April.
The clause stipulates that Mexico demonstrate an increased commitment to democracy and human rights as a condition for EU agreement to the trade accord.
But Mexican Foreign Minister Jose Angel Gurria said any differences between the two sides had nothing to do with the clause.
"That has never been a problem," Reforma newspaper quoted him as saying. He said difficulties had been of a commerical nature, but they had all been resolved.
Mexico and the EU are scheduled to sign an interim agreement for a commercial accord in Brussels on Wednesday.

Jacques Lecomte, head of the EU's delegation to Mexico, said the 15 nation bloc was greatly encouraged by the July 6 vote, which ushered in a new era of multi-party politics after seven decades of one-party rule.

But he said the EU's assessment of how well Mexico was fulfilling the democracy clause, also an EU condition in EU trade talks with Chile and South American trade bloc Mercosur, would not be tied just to the election result.
"The elections...represent an important step for democracy in Mexico, but there is no relation between this and the commercial agreement," Reforma quoted him as saying.
Instead, rather than basing its assessment on a single factor, the EU would look at Mexico's performance on a broader scale, he said.
Dutch ambassador Gerben Meihuzen said negotiations for a definitive trade agreement between the EU and Mexico would not be easy due to sensitivities in the agricultural sector.
"We will have some sensitive products, as is the case for agriculture," he said.
